import sympy as sp

# Define constants
R = 1200 * 10**3  # radius in meters
rho = 12.8 * 10**3  # density in kg/m^3 (converted from g/cm^3)
specific_heat = 0.400 * 1000  # specific heat in J/(kg*K)
flux_density = 10**11  # neutrinos/(s*cm^2)
energy_per_neutrino = 8 * 10**-14  # energy in Joules

# Calculate the cross-sectional area of the inner core
cross_sectional_area = sp.pi * R**2  # in m^2

# Calculate the power generated by the neutrinos
P = cross_sectional_area * energy_per_neutrino * flux_density  # in Watts (J/s)

# Calculate the change in energy required to heat the inner core by 1 degree Celsius
# Q = mcΔT
Delta_T = 1  # in K
Delta_Q = rho * (4/3) * sp.pi * R**3 * specific_heat * Delta_T  # in Joules

# Calculate the time to heat up by 1 degree Celsius
# P * t = Delta_Q => t = Delta_Q / P
time_to_heat = Delta_Q / P  # in seconds

# Express time in the form 1 x 10^N
N = sp.log(time_to_heat, 10).simplify()  # get the exponent

# Assign the integer value of N to result
result = sp.floor(N)

solution:
The cross sectional area is $\pi r^{2}$, so the incoming power generated by the neutrinos is:
$$
P=\pi r^{2} E \Phi
$$

where $E$ is the energy of each neutrino and $\Phi$ is the flux density. We want to cause a change in energy of:

$$
\Delta Q=m c \Delta T=\rho \frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3} c \Delta T
$$

which can be accomplished in a time:

$$
P t=\Delta Q \Longrightarrow t=\frac{\rho\left(4 \pi r^{3}\right) c \Delta T}{3 \pi r^{2} E \Phi}=\frac{4 \rho r c \Delta T}{3 E \Phi}=1 \times 10^{14} \mathrm{~s}
$$
